heading: INT. COMMUNITY BREAD COOPERATIVE - FORMER BUS DEPOT - MORNING

units.text: INT. COMMUNITY BREAD COOPERATIVE - FORMER BUS DEPOT - MORNING
A long concrete bay where city buses once slept.
Now: flour-dusted steel tables, a brick oven bolted into the old inspection pit, strings of laundry-line bunting.
Tall windows turn the light the color of weak tea.
The air smells of yeast and diesel ghosts.
ANSELMA DUARTE, 60s, forearms like rolled dough, sleeves shoved up, scores loaves with a razor blade.
She works without hurry.
TOMASZ WIERZBA, 30s, soft-spoken, rimless glasses, weighs flour on a brass scale and writes numbers in a battered notebook.
HADIYA BELLO, 20s, apron over a nursing-school sweatshirt, shapes rolls and yawns between each one.
Do we have enough rye for Thursday?
units.name: HADIYA

units.text: I counted four sacks.
units.name: TOMASZ

units.text: Three. Mrs. Pruitt took one for her church.
units.name: ANSELMA

units.text: She didn't ask.
units.name: TOMASZ

units.text: She never does.
units.name: ANSELMA

units.text: Three is fine. Thursday's mostly sourdough.
units.name: HADIYA

units.text: Thursday is the wedding.
units.name: TOMASZ

units.text: Thursday is the wedding and the school order.
units.name: ANSELMA

units.text: Then we need more rye.
units.name: HADIYA

units.text: Then we need to call the mill.
units.name: TOMASZ

units.text: The mill doesn't answer before ten.
units.name: ANSELMA

units.text: It's nine-forty.
units.name: HADIYA

units.text: Then we wait twenty minutes. Bread has taught me this.
units.name: ANSELMA

units.text: Nobody argues.
The oven ticks.
Hadiya sets another roll on the tray.
The big bay door rattles.
Light floods the floor.
WINSTON FAIRWEATHER-LEE, 70s, cardigan, cane, a tote bag of library books, steps through.
He squints up at the rafters like a man visiting a former church.
I drove a Number 14 out of this depot for thirty-one years.
units.name: WINSTON

units.text: We know, Winston. You tell us every Tuesday.
units.name: ANSELMA

units.text: It's Wednesday.
units.name: WINSTON

units.text: He's right, it's Wednesday.
units.name: TOMASZ

units.text: Then why does it feel like Tuesday?
units.name: HADIYA

units.text: Because Tuesday's bread was better.
units.name: ANSELMA

units.text: They've kept the pit.
units.name: WINSTON

units.text: The pit's the oven now.
units.name: TOMASZ

units.text: Mm. Good use of a pit.
units.name: WINSTON

units.text: He sets a library book on the table.
Hadiya reads the spine, nods, hands him a warm roll.
He eats it in two bites.
The oven ticks again.
Anselma slides in another tray.
